title: The Midnight Express
subtitle: A passenger who was never on board
setting: The overnight express, Carlisle to Inverness
briefing: A sleeper compartment is found empty at Inverness. The ticket was collected, the bunk was slept in, the door was locked from inside, and the passenger, Hugh Aylward, is not on the train. Every external door was sealed between Carlisle and the first stop. The window in the compartment does not open far enough for a person to pass through.
solution: Aylward never boarded. His brother-in-law, the conductor Frank Doyle, collected the ticket, rumpled the bunk, and locked the compartment from the corridor with a staff key that leaves the internal bolt engaged. Aylward was already dead in Carlisle, and the impossible disappearance was manufactured to place the death on a moving train and outside the jurisdiction that was investigating him.

suspects.name: Frank Doyle
suspects.motive: Married to the missing man's sister, and named in the same investigation.

statements.question: Did the passenger board?
statements.text: He boarded at Carlisle. I clipped his ticket myself on the platform.

statements.question: How was the compartment secured?
statements.text: Bolted from within. I had to use the emergency release at Inverness.

statements.question: Who holds a staff key?
statements.text: Myself, the sleeper attendant, and the guard. Three of us.

suspects.name: Rosa Lind
suspects.motive: Was disciplined after a complaint made by the missing man last year.

statements.question: Did the passenger board?
statements.text: I never saw him. I saw a made bunk and a closed door and I left it alone.

statements.question: How was the compartment secured?
statements.text: The door was shut before we left Carlisle. That is unusual, they normally settle in slowly.

statements.question: Who holds a staff key?
statements.text: Three of us on this service. Frank, myself, and the guard.

suspects.name: Alec Munro
suspects.motive: Signed the seal record that makes the disappearance impossible.

statements.question: Did the passenger board?
statements.text: I was at the rear. I would not see a boarding at coach C.

statements.question: How was the compartment secured?
statements.text: I did not go near it until Inverness.

statements.question: Who holds a staff key?
statements.text: The three of us. Mine has not left my belt.

suspects.name: Moira Doyle
suspects.motive: Inherits control of a disputed family trust.

statements.question: Did the passenger board?
statements.text: Frank told me Hugh was aboard. I did not see him myself.

statements.question: How was the compartment secured?
statements.text: I have no idea. I was four carriages away.

statements.question: Who holds a staff key?
statements.text: I am a passenger. I hold a ticket.

locations.name: Compartment C7
locations.description: A slept-in bunk, a locked door, and a window that opens four inches.

searchables.label: Examine the bunk
searchables.flavour: Rumpled from above, not slept in from within.

searchables.label: Examine the internal bolt
searchables.flavour: Engaged, with a fresh scrape on the housing.

searchables.label: Examine the window
searchables.flavour: Four inches, and the restraint is undamaged.

locations.name: Coach C Corridor
locations.description: The passage outside C7, and the only route to the door.

searchables.label: Examine the corridor lock
searchables.flavour: A staff key can throw the internal bolt from outside.

searchables.label: Ask the neighbouring passengers
searchables.flavour: Nobody in C6 or C8 heard anyone arrive.

locations.name: Carlisle Platform
locations.description: Where the train stood for eleven minutes at ten past midnight.

searchables.label: Review the platform camera
searchables.flavour: Every boarding passenger, and not one of them is Aylward.

searchables.label: Check the ticket collection record
searchables.flavour: Clipped at 12:08 AM, at the barrier.

locations.name: Guard's Van
locations.description: Seals, logs, and the paperwork that makes the train a sealed box.

searchables.label: Check the door seals
searchables.flavour: Intact, every one, all the way to Inverness.

searchables.label: Read the key sign-out log
searchables.flavour: Three keys, and one entry altered.

locations.name: Carlisle Sidings
locations.description: Where the search was extended after the second day.

searchables.label: Search the sidings
searchables.flavour: A discarded overcoat, well away from the platform.

evidence.name: Bunk disturbed from above
evidence.description: The bedding was rumpled by hand rather than slept in.

evidence.name: Scrape on the bolt housing
evidence.description: Fresh tooling marks where the internal bolt meets its housing.

evidence.name: Intact window restraint
evidence.description: The window opens four inches and the restraint is undamaged.

evidence.name: Staff key mechanism
evidence.description: A staff key can throw the internal bolt from the corridor side.

evidence.name: Neighbouring passengers
evidence.description: Nobody in C6 or C8 heard anyone enter C7 at any point.

evidence.name: Platform camera
evidence.description: The platform camera records every boarding, and Aylward is not among them.

evidence.name: Ticket collection record
evidence.description: The ticket was clipped at the barrier at 12:08 AM.

evidence.name: Intact door seals
evidence.description: Every external door seal is unbroken from Carlisle to Inverness.

evidence.name: Altered key log
evidence.description: One entry in the key sign-out log has been overwritten.

evidence.name: Discarded overcoat
evidence.description: The missing man's overcoat, found in the Carlisle sidings.

evidence.name: Phone location record
evidence.description: The passenger's phone never moved out of Carlisle.

evidence.name: Shared investigation file
evidence.description: The conductor is named alongside the missing man in an ongoing enquiry.

timeline.text: A ticket in Aylward's name is clipped at the barrier.
The door of C7 is observed already closed.
External door seals are checked and recorded intact.
C7 is opened with the emergency release.

hints: An impossible disappearance is usually an impossible arrival.
Check whether the passenger was ever recorded boarding, not merely ticketed.
Ask what a staff key can do that a passenger key cannot.
